video_title: Crypto’s Next Winners Won’t Be Blockchains
gist: Austin Barack of Relayer Capital lays out a cash-flow-driven framework for liquid crypto tokens, walking through a bottom-up burn model that values Venice's VVV at ~$43.90 versus ~$16 spot, plus theses on Pump trading at 5x buybacks, Ether.fi's shift from restaking to a neo-brokerage, and Hyperliquid's RWA markets. His overarching call: execution-layer infra is done as the revenue center, and the enduring tokens of this cycle will be applications and money.

insights.claim: Relayer Capital has moved from roughly a 50/50 liquid-versus-venture time split in the first three quarters of 2024 to spending 95% of its time on liquid tokens, because current venture dealflow is dominated by growth-stage payments and fintech companies rather than early compelling crypto-native bets.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Signals that sophisticated crypto capital sees better risk-adjusted entry in listed tokens than in private rounds — a headwind for late-stage crypto venture marks and a tailwind for liquid token flows.
insights.quote: So, at this point, it's like 95% liquid where I'm spending my time.

insights.claim: The core screen for liquid crypto positions is the intersection of growth and value — assets compounding fast that are also priced cheaply — a combination that exists in crypto only because capital flows are violently cyclical and leave assets oversold for extended periods.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Gives a repeatable screen: rank tokens on revenue/buyback growth rate against buyback-to-market-cap multiple, and buy where both are extreme.
insights.quote: no one comes to crypto because they're looking to find a company that's, you know, growing 10% a year and trading at a 4x multiple

insights.claim: Venture and liquid investing require opposite pricing discipline in crypto: on the venture side the best deals are essentially never cheap, so the only edge is entering at pre-seed or seed where absolute valuation is low, while liquid investing can demand both growth and cheapness.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Explains why paying up at seed can still be rational and why the same investor can refuse to pay up in liquid markets — useful for reading fund behavior.
insights.quote: it's very rare that the best deals are also priced cheaply

insights.claim: A prolonged deep bear market has compressed the investable liquid universe from around 100 tokens to roughly five or ten that show real product-market fit, fast growth and attractive pricing simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Argues for extreme concentration rather than basket exposure in liquid crypto portfolios.

insights.claim: An innings framework for cycle sequencing places the bottom as the first inning, the first broad asset recovery as the second, and onchain-yield protocols such as Athena and Pendle as third-inning assets that benefit most once onchain yields rise.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Gives a rotation map: after majors move, native yield protocols are the next leg to own.
insights.quote: Athena's up 40% in the last like 30 hours or something.

insights.claim: Bitcoin ripped from roughly $62,000 to almost $80,000 in the week of recording, which the host frames as the potential end of the bear market and therefore the last week to buy liquid tokens at bear-market prices.
insights.speaker: David (host)
insights.so_what: Anchors the price context for every valuation discussed in the episode and marks the moment the negative-drift regime may have flipped.

insights.claim: Venice is modeled as run-rating roughly $107 million of annualized revenue and $8.3 million of annualized token burns as of August, scaling to a projected $336 million of revenue and $70 million of burns in 2027.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: These are the hard inputs to check against onchain burn data — if burns track toward $70m the price target holds, if they stall the thesis breaks.
insights.quote: run rating at an in my estimate at 107 million of annualized revenue and um at 8.3 million of annualized births

insights.claim: A $43.90 price target for VVV is derived by applying a 50x multiple to $70 million of 2027 burns for a $3.5 billion token value, divided by projected end-of-2027 token supply, against a spot price of about $16 and about $12 when the model was last updated.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: A ~2.7x from spot on stated assumptions; the multiple and the burn line are the two variables to stress-test.

insights.claim: Buybacks-to-market-cap is proposed as the token equivalent of a P/E ratio, and a 50x multiple is called reasonable-to-cheap for a business growing directionally 5 to 10x year-over-year when compared with stock market comps.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Gives a single cross-token comparability metric — apply it to Pump, Hyperliquid and Ether.fi to spot dislocations.

insights.claim: Headline burn-as-percent-of-revenue figures are misleading because burns must be assessed against gross margin and opex: an 8% burn on revenue at 50% gross margins and 10% EBITDA margins means the company is burning the majority of its free cash flow.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: A screen for whether a token's buyback program is sustainable or is quietly starving reinvestment.

insights.claim: Venice's credit-purchase product, which did not exist eight months before recording and launched in January or February, is already run-rating at $60 million of ARR and its burns are trackable onchain.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Demonstrated ability to stand up a nine-figure-run-rate revenue line in under a year is the empirical basis for underwriting the unlaunched Mines product.
insights.quote: So a product that didn't exist 8 months ago is now doing 60 million year of revenue.

insights.claim: The single most fragile assumption in the VVV model is that $29 million of the projected $70 million of 2027 burns comes from the not-yet-live Mines product — roughly 40% of forecast burns from a product with no revenue history.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: The clean bear case: strip Mines out and fair value falls roughly 40% on the burn line.
insights.quote: That's 40% of 2027 burns coming from a new product.

insights.claim: The model also assumes burn rates themselves ratchet up over time, with the credit-purchase burn rising from 5% of every purchase today to 10% by 2027, plus a new subscription-renewal burn beginning late this year or early Q1.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Two policy changes, not just growth, are embedded in the target — announcements of renewal burns or a higher credit burn rate are the catalysts to watch.

insights.claim: The author rates his own Venice model a six out of ten on an optimism scale where zero is the ultimate bear case, five is base case and ten is the full bull case.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Self-declared optimism bias means the $43.90 target should be haircut rather than treated as a base case.
insights.quote: You can probably call it like a I would call it a six.

insights.claim: Venice's growth has run far ahead of expectations: from roughly 1 million users and an estimated $10-20 million revenue range at the start of the year to about 4 million historical users and a 5-10x revenue increase in eight months.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Establishes the growth rate that justifies the premium multiple; a deceleration in user or credit growth is the first sell signal.

insights.claim: Venice is presented as one of the very few crypto products with legitimate mainstream consumer crossover and genuine product-market fit, monetizing through $18, $68 and $200 monthly subscription tiers plus overage credit purchases.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Consumer AI revenue gives VVV a non-crypto demand driver that most tokens lack.
insights.quote: we've seen so few products in crypto that have legitimate mainstream consumer crossover that have found product market fit and Venice is is one of those

themes.theme: Mines as an AI app store

insights.claim: Venice's Mines product is described as an app-store layer for AI where power users package structured multi-model prompt workflows for average users and earn a kickback when their creation is used, mirroring the Apple App Store developer model.
insights.speaker: David (host)
insights.so_what: If it works, it converts Venice from a subscription business into a platform with a supply-side flywheel and third-party distribution.

insights.claim: Venice's structural advantage over generalized model aggregators is that it owns the direct end-user relationship, which is precisely what a developer-tooling router cannot monetize the same way.
insights.speaker: David (host)
insights.so_what: Frames the consumer-facing layer, not the routing layer, as where platform economics accrue in multi-model AI.
insights.quote: because Venice owns a direct relationship to the user

insights.claim: Mines' distribution advantage over ChatGPT's app-store attempt is placement: OpenAI's version was neither open nor prominently featured, while Venice plans to feature Mines in the middle of everything it builds, with an incentivized seven-figure active user base marketing to each other on Twitter, Reddit, Telegram and Discord.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Placement plus creator incentives is the testable mechanism for whether the $29m Mines burn assumption converts.

insights.claim: Diffusion-model creation — image and video — is flagged as the highest-value use case for a Mines-style app store because a novice trying to make a one-minute video has no idea where to start, unlike chat where prompt quality differences are invisible to the user.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Points to creator tooling, not chat, as the wedge — Venice's October film festival in New York is the visible push behind it.

insights.claim: The upside case for Mines may be indirect: rather than generating its own revenue line, it could accelerate subscription growth and credit purchases by making the existing product more useful, meaning the revenue attribution in the model could be wrong even if the direction is right.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Watch total credit burn rather than Mines-specific revenue when judging whether the launch worked.

insights.claim: The Open Router outcome — a raise at a $1.3 billion valuation roughly two months earlier followed by a reported $7 billion Stripe acquisition at more than 7x that mark — is read as validation of a multi-model routing world and as evidence that the right comparable multiple for Venice may be 70x rather than 30x or 50x.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: A live private-market comp that directly supports multiple expansion on the VVV target.

insights.claim: Venice is held up as one of the most elegant token-equity balances in crypto: the operating business is off-chain and funded by equity because running a fully onchain business is operationally complex, while the token captures value through programmatic onchain burns on new signups and credit purchases.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: A template for judging dual token-equity structures: does the equity fund operations while the token gets the free cash flow claim?

insights.claim: Venice raised $65 million of equity and token at a $1 billion valuation specifically so it could prioritize token burns while still reinvesting in growth — having raised roughly 10-20x more than the few million dollars burned to date.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Explains how an early-stage company can run buybacks without starving growth, and sets the bar for other token issuers claiming the same.
insights.quote: they raised $65 million so that they'd have the ability to prioritize the token but also be able to actively reinvest in the business

insights.claim: Until the Clarity Act passes, token holders have no guarantee that value built in the equity entity accrues to the token, so issuers must demonstrably 'walk the walk' with programmatic burns to earn trust — making pre-legislation buyback behavior a credibility signal rather than a valuation input alone.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Regulatory clarity is a re-rating catalyst across dual-structure tokens; until then, discount discretionary buyback promises.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid's roughly 99% buyback ratio is called an anomaly that is not sustainable long term unless all customer acquisition is funded by Trade XYZ or the team, with a drift toward 90-95% expected so cash can be redirected to marketing.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: A reduction in Hyperliquid's buyback ratio would be normal rather than bearish, but would compress the buyback multiple mechanically.

insights.claim: Locking VVV mints DEM, a tokenized compute token that grants roughly one dollar per day of inference, and Venice split this from VVV around August after originally using a single token for both inference and value capture.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Tokenized compute is a customer-acquisition subsidy funded by token lockups — a mechanism worth watching as a template for other AI tokens.

insights.claim: Tokens as an asset class have had negative capital drift for roughly 18 months as money left crypto for equities and AI, and this drift is cyclical rather than structural and has probably just flipped — meaning every fundamentally-driven token gets a flows tailwind independent of its own business.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: The single largest beta call in the episode: if flows have turned, fundamentally-cheap tokens get both earnings growth and multiple expansion.
insights.quote: tokens have had negative drift for the last 18 months

insights.claim: Fundamentally-driven tokens are partially coupled and partially decoupled from crypto beta, and the decoupling has been positive — cash-generative businesses with returned value have a floor valuation that let them re-rate during a period when Bitcoin and ETH were flat to down.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Justifies holding revenue tokens as a lower-drawdown way to stay long crypto rather than as pure beta substitutes.

insights.claim: Pump and Hyperliquid carry extra reflexivity to crypto beta that Venice lacks, because their fundamentals are directly driven by onchain activity, memecoin trading and crypto trading volume, while Venice's equivalent tide is AI adoption.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Sizes the beta: own Pump/Hype for leveraged exposure to a crypto risk-on turn, own Venice for uncorrelated AI-adoption exposure.

insights.claim: Pump's revenue over the last 90 days has grown about 80% versus the 90-day average, and a further doubling or tripling from here is plausible on a return of onchain activity and memecoin trading.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: A concrete, trackable revenue forecast — Pump fee data is public and can falsify or confirm it within a quarter.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid's recent re-rating came from HIP-3 and RWA market volume — commodities, stocks and indices — that generates almost no revenue because those markets are in growth mode, while the actual cash cow remains the higher-take-rate crypto token business.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Price has moved on volume that does not monetize — the real earnings upside only arrives if crypto trading flows return.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid fee generation jumped from roughly just under $1 million a day a week before recording to about $5 million in a single day a couple of days before recording.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: A roughly 5x daily fee spike is the live evidence for the reflexivity claim and a leading indicator to monitor daily.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid is becoming a price-discovery venue for pre-IPO and newly listed equities including SpaceX, Cerebras and Unitree, to the point that IPO bankers will increasingly look at a Hyperliquid screen when setting price.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: If onchain perps become a reference price for traditional IPO pricing, Hyperliquid's addressable market extends well beyond crypto trading fees.
insights.quote: I think increasingly bankers as they set what the price for an IPO should be are going to look at their Hyperlquid screen

insights.claim: Pump trades at roughly 5x buybacks while Hyperliquid and Lighter trade in the 30-40x range, a gap attributed to perceived revenue durability rather than actual cash generation, with 10x called much more reasonable — implying a 2x from current levels assuming zero further growth.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: The most explicit relative-value trade in the episode: long Pump on multiple convergence, with growth as free optionality.
insights.quote: It's trading at 5x buybacks where if you look at you know hyperlquid and lighter in the 30 to 40x buybacks range.

insights.claim: The bear case on Pump is the OpenSea analogy — billions in revenue followed by a roughly 95% collapse twelve months later — but two-plus years of durable and growing Pump revenue is evidence that memecoin trading is a persistent business rather than a fad.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Reframes the core objection that keeps the multiple compressed; durability data is the catalyst for re-rating.

insights.claim: Crypto Twitter, liquid funds and most retail investors have surprisingly little overlap with actual memecoin traders, which is why they persistently disbelieve Pump's revenue numbers — once you accept you are not the target user, the durability makes sense.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: A generalizable sourcing error: professional investors under-price consumer businesses whose users they never meet.

insights.claim: Memecoin trading should be valued as a speculation and gambling business comparable to Wynn, Las Vegas Sands, MGM, DraftKings, FanDuel, prediction markets, lotteries and zero-day-to-expiry options on Robinhood — negative expected value for the aggregate user base does not stop the business from being large and durable.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Supplies the comp set for repricing Pump against listed gaming multiples rather than crypto infra multiples.
insights.quote: If like for the total user base it's negative EV, that doesn't mean that you won't use it because then lotteryies shouldn't be like the massive business that they are.

insights.claim: Pump's buyback commitment is a live governance risk: it moved from an unguaranteed 100% of revenue to a guaranteed 50% for twelve months subject to renewal next year, and how one handicaps that renewal swings the fair buyback multiple between roughly 6-10x and 10-14x.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: The renewal decision is a dated, binary catalyst with roughly a two-turn multiple swing attached to it.

insights.claim: More than 65% of Ether.fi's revenue now comes from its neo-bank product — credit card usage and borrow revenue — with only 35% from yield and staking, and the staking share is shrinking, yet the market still values it as a liquid restaking business.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: A classic misclassification trade: the business mix has already flipped while the comp set has not, leaving it at roughly 10-15x earnings.
insights.quote: today 65 plus% of Ether's business comes from their Neo Bank product

insights.claim: Ether.fi fell more than 10% alongside Lido on the day of the Ethereum inflation reduction proposal, which is offered as direct evidence that the market still misprices it as a staking-correlated asset.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Staking-headline selloffs in Ether.fi are buyable dislocations if the mix-shift thesis is right.

insights.claim: Ether.fi's credit card volume has gone from about $300,000 a day a year ago to $3-4 million a day, a 10x year-over-year that is still described as a tiny absolute number with hockey-stick potential ahead.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: The single cleanest KPI for the thesis — daily card volume is trackable and drives interchange-funded buybacks.
insights.quote: a year ago, they were doing $300,000 of credit card volume a day. Now, they're doing 3 to 4 million a day

insights.claim: Blockworks modeled $21 million of Ether.fi buy-and-burns over the next twelve months while halving current growth rates for conservatism; applying roughly $30 million of buybacks at a 30x neo-brokerage multiple implies a token price over $1, roughly 2x from current levels before any multiple expansion.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: A second explicit price target with a named third-party model to cross-check against.

insights.claim: The majority of Ether.fi's token supply is already fully circulating, so with programmatic buybacks running there is structural buy pressure and almost no emissions offset — a supply profile closer to an equity like Microsoft than to most crypto tokens.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Low remaining unlock overhang is a rare and underpriced feature; screen tokens on circulating-supply completeness before buying any buyback story.

insights.claim: Interest income on borrows is only about 4% of Ether.fi's revenue today with roughly $20 million of user borrowing, versus 60-70% at Nubank, marking the mix shift as the main growth vector rather than card interchange itself.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Quantifies the gap to a mature neo-bank P&L — borrow revenue growth is the metric that would justify a much higher multiple.
insights.quote: If you look at Etherfi today, it's still very early. It's 4%.

insights.claim: Ether.fi replaced its own bespoke lending arrangements with a dedicated Aave v4 instance under an 80/20 revenue share in its favor, letting a lean team run a best-in-class borrow-lend product at very low cost.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Evidence that DeFi composability is now a real cost advantage for consumer fintech, and a new distribution channel for Aave.

insights.claim: The modern startup pattern on display is to stay small and rent big technologies: Ether.fi could evolve from neo-bank to neo-brokerage at almost no incremental cost because tokenized stocks and real-world assets already existed on Ethereum, requiring no new business arm.
insights.speaker: David (host)
insights.so_what: Predicts unusually high operating leverage in onchain consumer apps — margins should expand as they add product lines.
insights.quote: don't have a big team and instead use big technologies

insights.claim: The bull comparison for Ether.fi is Nubank, worth roughly $80 billion with 139 million users, on the argument that both offer more consumer-friendly and internet-native products globally — with Ether.fi doing it in a stablecoin-driven onchain context.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Sets the ceiling case: capturing a fraction of Nubank's outcome would be a many-multiple return from a sub-$1 token.
insights.quote: New Bank is worth, you know, like $80 billion and has 139 million users

insights.claim: Execution-layer infrastructure once generated over 95% of total crypto revenue; applications now generate about two-thirds with execution layers at one-third, and the trend is expected to continue until applications produce 90%-plus of crypto revenue.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: The core allocation call of the episode: rotate out of L1/L2 tokens and into application tokens that capture fees.
insights.quote: now it's actually applications are generating about 2/3 of revenue and about a third is generated by execution layers

insights.claim: The enduring tokens of the next cycle will be applications and money, not blockchains — excitement around new layer ones and layer twos is described as mostly a thing of the past.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Reframes portfolio construction into exactly two buckets and implies persistent multiple compression for chain tokens.
insights.quote: I think we're going to find the most enduring tokens be applications and money.

insights.claim: Zcash is framed as serving a different type of user and embodying crypto's original ethos, which explains why it is resonating with OG Bitcoin holders and seeing structural inflows.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Identifies a specific, non-momentum flow source for privacy money assets in the money bucket.

insights.claim: ETH is newly interesting as money rather than as a revenue asset, because of quantum risk to Bitcoin, concentrated Bitcoin ownership and Strategy-related ownership risk — a reversal from a prior view that Ethereum looked quite overvalued on revenue.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: A non-consensus reason to own ETH that is independent of L1 fee revenue and would re-rate on any Bitcoin-specific risk event.
insights.quote: So it actually makes me more curious about like Ethereum from a money perspective than I've been in a very long time.

insights.claim: Solana is the chain with the most onchain activity and the most spot volume and is what enables Pump, but it is going through a transition where high utilization is not converting into revenue because the MEV it once captured has gone away.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Usage-versus-monetization divergence is the key thing to watch on Solana; it is called one of the most compelling bets on crypto adoption despite weak fee capture.
insights.quote: Salana is what's enabling Pump. It has the most spot activity on chain.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid is presented as the clearest expression of the original crypto thesis playing out — instant settlement, 24/7 trading, all assets onchain, and the financial system shifting onto blockchains.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Defines 24/7 trading and tokenization as one of the two investable meta-themes alongside crypto-x-AI.

insights.claim: Highly utilized consumer-facing crypto surfaces now include Base and Robinhood alongside Ethereum, indicating that distribution-rich front ends rather than new chains are where activity is concentrating.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: Reinforces the application-layer rotation and points at incumbent-distribution venues as the activity aggregators.

insights.claim: Looking back on this period, the cycle is expected to be remembered as the era of zero-to-one applications that connected crypto to the rest of the world plus the money assets that resonated, with 2026 seen retrospectively as offering good entry points in Venice, Hyperliquid, Pump, Ether.fi, Bitcoin and Zcash.
insights.speaker: Austin Barack
insights.so_what: The explicit consolidated watchlist from the episode — six names framed as the cycle's winners.
